forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Tonbridge and Malling salaries budget £71,150 overspent at end of September, mostly agency cover
news_drafts.lead:
Tonbridge and Malling Borough Council's salaries budget was overspent by £71,150 at the end of September 2026, according to a report from its Head of Finance to the Finance, Regeneration and Property Scrutiny Select Committee. Spending on salaries to September was £7,713,550, against a budget for the period of £7,642,400.

The report says the overspend is mainly agency staff cover in Planning and Legal Services. Agency costs cover sickness and vacancies in those two services. The report also says that extending two posts in Executive Services adds cost.

The report describes the position as "an overspend (adverse variance) of £71,150". The committee meets on 17 November 2026.

news_drafts.headline: Tonbridge and Malling's £2.8m forecast funding gap eliminated, with a balanced 2026-27 budget approved
news_drafts.lead:
Tonbridge and Malling Borough Council no longer forecasts a funding gap over its planning period, according to its external auditor's annual report. The gap was £2.8m for 2025-26 in the council's medium-term financial strategy (its financial plan for the next few years, showing the gap between expected spending and expected income). The council has approved a balanced budget for 2026-27.

The auditor, the accountancy firm Grant Thornton, says the gap was eliminated "following a more favourable funding settlement, updated financial assumptions and continued prudent financial management". The council has also achieved £5.1m in savings and transformation contributions before 2025-26. It no longer needs a standalone savings and transformation strategy.

The report says the council is now making planned contributions to its reserves (money put aside for the unexpected or for a named purpose) rather than drawing on them to balance future budgets.
news_drafts.paper_title: Annex 1 - Grant Thornton Annual Audit Report

news_drafts.headline: Tonbridge and Malling rates savings-target risk 20 out of 25 before controls and 9 after, register shows
news_drafts.lead:
Tonbridge and Malling Borough Council scores the risk of missing its savings and transformation targets at 20 on a 25-point scale before any controls are applied, falling to 9 once its current measures are counted. The figures come from an example entry in the risk register format set out for its Audit Committee meeting on 28 September 2026.

The entry says that failing to meet the targets would lead to an overspend with a significant effect on the council's reserves (money put aside, here as a cushion for the unexpected). In the register's wording, that could result in a "Section 114 notice" (a formal warning from the chief finance officer that the council cannot balance its budget, which freezes new spending until councillors agree a plan) declaring the authority "no longer a Going Concern". Before controls, likelihood is scored 4 out of 5 and impact 5 out of 5. With controls, both are scored 3.

The council's stated control is ongoing review of its Savings and Transformation Strategy and its medium-term financial strategy (its financial plan for the next three to five years) by councillors and officers. The register shows the risk was first identified in April 2017 and last reviewed in March 2025.

findings.committee: Finance, Regeneration and Property Scrutiny Select Committee
findings.headline: Land Charges income to end of September 2026 was £84,220 against a budget to date of £111,100, a variance of £26,880.
findings.detail: Land Charges is the only line in the central group. The paper shows actual income below the budget to date.
findings.matters: It is one of the few income lines in the statement running below budget, and the variance is small relative to the garden waste shortfall.
findings.figures: Annual budget £201,500; budget to end of September £111,100; actual to end of September £84,220; variance £26,880

findings.committee: Finance, Regeneration and Property Scrutiny Select Committee
findings.headline: Planning Applications income to end of September 2026 was £634,300 against a budget to date of £576,000, £58,300 above budget.
findings.detail: Planning Applications is the largest income line in the planning, housing and regulatory services group. The paper shows it above budget to date.
findings.matters: Planning fee income is a sensitive development-related revenue line, and running ahead of budget at the half-year point is a result another council's finance officer could compare against.
findings.figures: Annual budget £1,151,000; budget to end of September £576,000; actual to end of September £634,300; variance £58,300 above budget

findings.committee: Finance, Regeneration and Property Scrutiny Select Committee
findings.headline: Long Stay Car Parking income to end of September 2026 was £559,119 against a budget to date of £492,000, £67,119 above budget.
findings.detail: This is the largest favourable variance among the individual lines in the statement. The paper shows it as income above budget to date.
findings.matters: Car parking income running above budget offsets part of the garden waste shortfall, which a finance director would weigh when assessing the street scene income position.
findings.figures: Annual budget £982,000; budget to end of September £492,000; actual to end of September £559,119; variance £67,119 above budget

findings.committee: Finance, Regeneration and Property Scrutiny Select Committee
findings.headline: Recycling Performance Payment shows £0 income to end of September 2026 against an annual budget of £700,000, with no amount profiled to date.
findings.detail: The line has no budget to date and no actual to date. The statement does not explain the timing of this income.
findings.matters: A £700,000 annual income line showing nothing received at the half-year point is a material timing question for any council budgeting on this stream.
findings.figures: Annual budget £700,000; budget to end of September £0; actual to end of September £0

findings.committee: Finance, Regeneration and Property Scrutiny Select Committee
findings.headline: Garden Waste Collection income to end of September 2026 was £1,983,769 against a budget to date of £2,246,000, a variance of £262,231.
findings.detail: This is the largest single variance in the statement. The budget to date is higher than the full-year budget shown on the same line, and actual income to September already exceeds the annual budget of £1,937,300.
findings.matters: Garden waste is the largest single income line in the statement, and the profiled budget sits above the annual figure on the same row, which a finance director would need to understand before judging the variance.
findings.figures: Annual budget £1,937,300; budget to end of September £2,246,000; actual to end of September £1,983,769; variance £262,231
